agent_report.discovery: Explored wp-admin and found need for content awareness - AI agents need to know what posts exist before helping with content management
agent_report.testing_results: Successfully tested via REST API. Returns post metadata including title, status, author, dates, excerpt, and comment count. Works for all authenticated users with edit_posts capability.
ideas: garden-abilities/get-post - Get full content of a specific post
lessons_learned: Input schemas with no required params need 'default': {} to work via GET
Chat widget uses closed Shadow DOM - test via REST API first
Use existing categories (site, user) or register custom ones first

agent_report.discovery: Explored Site Health page (Tools → Site Health) and found valuable diagnostic data hidden multiple clicks deep. Critical issues, security concerns, and performance recommendations are exactly what AI agents need for proactive monitoring.
agent_report.testing_results: Successfully tested via REST API. Returns overall_status (good/should_be_improved/critical), summary counts, critical_issues array, recommendations array, and passed_tests array. Requires view_site_health_checks capability.
ideas: garden-abilities/site-health-info - Return debug info tab data (PHP version, database info, etc.)
garden-abilities/plugin-status - Check for plugin updates and security issues
garden-abilities/theme-status - Analyze active and inactive themes
garden-abilities/error-log - Read recent PHP errors from debug.log
lessons_learned: Admin-only functions like get_core_updates() need manual require_once when running via REST
Some Site Health tests make slow HTTP requests - skip them for faster response
Wrap test execution in try/catch for graceful degradation
The Site Health API is powerful but underutilized - great opportunity for AI tools
